title: Returned-Payment Fee on a Respite or Trial Stay
content:
Every payment returned unpaid on a respite or trial stay carries one returned-payment fee, posted as an add-on on that stay and referencing the returned-payment entry. This applies to every stay under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement.

## What the fee posting does

- It records one add-on charge entry on the stay account — a returned-payment fee — for one payment that the bank returned unpaid.
- The entry references the returned-payment entry it arises from, so each returned payment on the stay's ledger can be matched with its own fee.
- It raises the stay balance by the fee; the guest sees the fee on the stay statement and a higher balance owed.

## One fee per returned payment

| Stay ledger shows | Returned-payment fees the stay carries |
|---|---|
| One returned payment | One, referencing that returned-payment entry |
| Two returned payments | Two, each referencing its own returned-payment entry |

## How it is invoked

The fee is posted with the agent-side tool `post_returned_payment_fee_57d4cb7a`. The agent unlocks the tool and then calls it; one call records one fee entry, dated today.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `respite_stay_id` | Reference number of the respite or trial stay being charged, as returned by the stay lookup | Identifier |
| `source_entry_id` | Reference number of the returned-payment entry the fee arises from, as returned by the stay ledger lookup | Identifier |
| `fee_amount` | Amount of the fee in USD | Positive number with 2 decimal places, already rounded half up to the cent |

## Return

A confirmation sentence naming the new fee entry reference number, the stay reference number, the returned-payment entry referenced, the fee in USD with 2 decimal places and the resulting stay balance. A returned entry reference number means the fee was posted.
